# Nomad node pool specification

Node pools group nodes, letting you restrict which jobs are able to place
allocations in a given set of nodes. Specify node pools as HCL files and submit
them with the [`nomad node pool apply`][pool-apply] CLI command. Unlike [job
specifications][jobspecs], node pool specifications do not support HCL2
features like functions.

This example is a node pool specification generated with the [`nomad node pool
init` command][pool-init].

```hcl
node_pool "example" {

  description = "Example node pool"

  # meta is optional metadata on the node pool, defined as key-value pairs.
  # The scheduler does not use node pool metadata as part of scheduling.
  meta {
    environment = "prod"
    owner       = "sre"
  }

  # node_identity_ttl is an optional parameter that sets the TTL for all node
  # identities issued to nodes in this node pool. The value must be a valid
  # duration string (e.g. "30m", "1h", "24h"). If not set, the default value is
  # "24h".
  # node_identity_ttl = "24h"

  # The scheduler configuration options specific to this node pool. This block
  # supports a subset of the fields supported in the global scheduler
  # configuration as described at:
  # https://developer.hashicorp.com/nomad/commands/operator/scheduler/set-config
  #
  # * scheduler_algorithm is the scheduling algorithm to use for the pool.
  #   If not defined, the global cluster scheduling algorithm is used.
  #
  # Available only in Nomad Enterprise.

  # scheduler_config {
  #   scheduler_algorithm = "spread"
  # }
}
```

Example usage if the above is in a file named `pool.nomad.hcl`:

```shell-session
$ nomad node pool apply ./pool.nomad.hcl
Successfully applied node pool "example"!
```

## Parameters

- `description` `(string: <optional>)` - Sets a human readable description for
  the node pool.

- `meta` `(map[string]string: <optional>)` - Sets optional metadata on the node
  pool, defined as key-value pairs. The scheduler does not use node pool
  metadata as part of scheduling.

- `node_identity_ttl` `(string: <optional>)` - Sets the TTL for node identities
  issued to nodes in this node pool. The value must be a valid duration string
  (e.g. "30m", "1h", "24h"). If not set, the default value is "24h".

- `scheduler_config` <code>([SchedulerConfig][sched-config]: nil)</code> <EnterpriseAlert inline /> -
  Sets scheduler configuration options specific to the node pool. If not
  defined, the global scheduler configurations are used.

- `batch_queue` <code>([BatchQueue][batch-queue]: nil)</code> - Configures a
  [batch job queue][] for the node pool. The queue holds the batch jobs
  registered in the node pool and sends them to the scheduler one at a time.
  Child jobs that a [periodic][] job launches do not enter the queue. If not
  defined, the node pool does not queue batch jobs. You cannot configure a
  batch job queue on the built-in `default` and `all` node pools.

### `scheduler_config` parameters <EnterpriseAlert inline />

- `scheduler_algorithm` `(string: <optional>)` - The [scheduler algorithm][]
  used for this node pool. Must be one of `binpack` or `spread`.

- `memory_oversubscription_enabled` `(bool: <optional>)` - The [memory
  oversubscription][] setting to use for this node pool.

### `batch_queue` parameters

The `batch_queue` block must contain one of the following blocks, which sets the
queue type.

- `fifo` <code>([Fifo][fifo]: nil)</code> - Configures a FIFO queue, which sends
  jobs to the scheduler in the order that you register them.

- `dynamic_priority` <code>([DynamicPriority][dynamic-priority]: nil)</code> -
  Configures a dynamic priority queue, which sends jobs to the scheduler in
  order of their adjusted priority. Refer to [Adjusted priority][] for how the
  queue calculates it.

- `constraint_timeout` `(string: <optional>)` - Specifies how long the queue
  waits for a job that Nomad cannot place because of its constraints, as a
  duration string such as `"5m"`. The timeout starts when the scheduler creates
  the job's blocked evaluation. When the timeout expires, the queue sends the
  next job to the scheduler, and the blocked job waits for placement outside the
  queue. If not set, the queue waits until Nomad places the job or you stop it.
  The timeout does not apply to jobs that wait for resources. Refer to [Head of
  line blocking][] for details.

  <!-- TODO(owner: Mike Smithhisler): constraint_timeout still ends the wait early at release/2.1.0-rc.1 (215402ecfd). A dev agent built from that branch with constraint_timeout = "30s" and "120s" placed the next job about two seconds after it was registered. The watcher logged "constraint failure" and then "shutting down workload watcher for job ... err=context canceled" in the same millisecond that the blocked evaluation was created. In WorkloadWatcher.wait in nomad/queues/queue/workload_watcher.go, the loop reassigns ctx with context.WithDeadline at line 122 and calls cancel at line 127, so the next WatchCtx call returns immediately. Commit 69097488a0 fixed the unset case, and the same dev agent held the queue for more than 90 seconds with no constraint_timeout until the blocked job was stopped. Confirm the fix for a set timeout before release. -->

This example configures a dynamic priority queue that treats each namespace as a
tenant.

```hcl
node_pool "batch" {
  description = "Clients that run batch workloads"

  batch_queue {
    dynamic_priority {
      calc_interval = "10s"

      tenant_fairshare {
        tenant_type   = "namespace"
        cpu_weight    = 25
        memory_weight = 25
      }

      age {
        weight = 10
        max    = "1h"
      }

      job_size {
        cpu_weight    = 10
        cpu_max       = 1000
        memory_weight = 10
        memory_max    = 1024
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### `fifo` parameters

The `fifo` block has no parameters. Specify an empty block.

```hcl
batch_queue {
  fifo {}
}
```

#### `dynamic_priority` parameters

- `calc_interval` `(string: <required>)` - Specifies how often the queue
  recalculates each tenant's fairshare and the adjusted priority of every queued
  job, as a duration string such as `"30s"`. Must be greater than zero.

- `tenant_fairshare` <code>([TenantFairshare][tenant-fairshare]: &lt;required&gt;)</code> -
  Configures how the queue groups jobs into tenants and how much each tenant's
  share of allocated resources affects the priority of its jobs.

- `age` <code>([Age][age]: &lt;required&gt;)</code> - Configures how much the
  time a job waits in the queue affects its priority. Specify an empty block,
  `age {}`, to leave job age out of the calculation.

- `job_size` <code>([JobSize][job-size]: &lt;required&gt;)</code> - Configures
  how much the resources that a job requests affect its priority. Specify an
  empty block, `job_size {}`, to leave job size out of the calculation.

<!-- TODO(owner: Mike Smithhisler): At release/2.1.0-rc.1 (215402ecfd), `nomad node pool apply` rejects a dynamic_priority block that omits the age or job_size block, or that omits cpu_weight or memory_weight in tenant_fairshare. api/batch_job_queue.go has a "validate and set sensible defaults" TODO. Confirm whether these stay required in 2.1. Also, BatchQueueConfig.Validate in nomad/structs/batch_queue.go accepts a batch_queue block that sets both fifo and dynamic_priority. A dev agent built from rc.1 applied such a block, and /v1/queue/jobs reported the type dynamic_priority. Confirm whether that is intended. -->

##### `tenant_fairshare` parameters

- `tenant_type` `(string: <required>)` - Specifies how the queue groups jobs into
  tenants. Must be one of `namespace` or `metadata`. With `namespace`, each
  namespace is a tenant. With `metadata`, each distinct value of the job
  [`meta`][meta] key named in `metadata_key` is a tenant, and jobs that do not
  set that key skip the queue.

- `metadata_key` `(string: "")` - Specifies the job `meta` key whose value
  identifies a job's tenant. Required when `tenant_type` is `metadata`.

- `cpu_weight` `(int: <required>)` - Specifies the maximum amount that a
  tenant's share of allocated CPU adds to the priority of its jobs. Tenants
  whose jobs hold a smaller share of the CPU allocated to batch jobs in the node
  pool receive more of this weight. If `0`, allocated CPU does not affect
  priority.

- `memory_weight` `(int: <required>)` - Specifies the maximum amount that a
  tenant's share of allocated memory adds to the priority of its jobs. Tenants
  whose jobs hold a smaller share of the memory allocated to batch jobs in the
  node pool receive more of this weight. If `0`, allocated memory does not affect
  priority.

- `exclude_alloc_statuses` `(array<string>: [])` - Specifies the allocation
  client statuses that the queue excludes when it adds up the resources
  allocated to each tenant. For example, `["failed", "lost"]` excludes failed
  and lost allocations. If empty, the queue counts every allocation of the
  tenant's batch jobs. Refer to [Tenant fairshare][] for details.

##### `age` parameters

- `weight` `(int: 0)` - Specifies the maximum amount that the time a job waits
  in the queue adds to its priority. If `0`, job age does not affect priority.
  Set `max` when you set this parameter. If `max` is not set, every job receives
  the full `weight` as soon as it enters the queue.

- `max` `(string: "")` - Specifies the wait time, as a duration string such as
  `"12h"`, at which a job receives the full `weight`.

##### `job_size` parameters

- `cpu_weight` `(int: 0)` - Specifies the maximum amount that a job's requested
  CPU adds to its priority. Jobs that request less CPU receive more of this
  weight. If `0`, requested CPU does not affect priority. Set `cpu_max` when you
  set this parameter. If `cpu_max` is not set, jobs that request CPU receive
  none of this weight.

- `cpu_max` `(int: 0)` - Specifies the requested CPU, in MHz, at or above which a
  job receives none of the `cpu_weight`. A job's requested CPU is the sum of
  each task's `cpu` resource multiplied by its group's `count`. A task that sets
  [`cores`][cores] instead of `cpu` adds `0` MHz to the sum.

- `memory_weight` `(int: 0)` - Specifies the maximum amount that a job's
  requested memory adds to its priority. Jobs that request less memory receive
  more of this weight. If `0`, requested memory does not affect priority. Set
  `memory_max` when you set this parameter. If `memory_max` is not set, jobs
  that request memory receive none of this weight.

- `memory_max` `(int: 0)` - Specifies the requested memory, in MB, at or above
  which a job receives none of the `memory_weight`. A job's requested memory is
  the sum of each task's `memory` resource multiplied by its group's `count`.
